q: Which DI lifetime should a DbContext normally have in ASP.NET Core?
explain: One DbContext per HTTP request: it is a unit of work and is not thread-safe.

q: A Singleton service takes a Scoped service in its constructor. What is this bug called?
explain: The scoped service is captured for the whole life of the app, so it is shared across requests.

options: Last on the request and first on the response
First on the request and last on the response
explain: Requests flow down in registration order and responses flow back up in reverse.

q: What does the CLR's JIT compiler do?
options: Turns IL into native machine code at run time
explain: Roslyn compiles C# to IL; the JIT turns IL into machine code when a method is first called.

q: Why avoid task.Result in ASP.NET code?
options: It blocks a thread and can deadlock or starve the thread pool
explain: Blocking on async code wastes threads and can deadlock where there is a synchronization context.

q: var q = list.Where(x => x > 1); list.Add(10); — when does the filter run?
explain: LINQ uses deferred execution: the query runs when you enumerate it, so it sees 10.

q: Which method throws if MORE than one element matches?
explain: Single and SingleOrDefault demand at most one match.

q: What fixes the N+1 query problem in EF Core?
explain: Eager loading or projection fetches related data in one query instead of one per row.
Records compare by value and support non-destructive copies with 'with'.

q: How should you create HttpClient instances in ASP.NET Core?
options: One static instance that never refreshes DNS
explain: The factory pools handlers: no socket exhaustion and DNS changes are respected.

q: Which configuration source wins by default?
explain: Later providers override earlier ones; environment variables (and command line) come late.
